item.title: Saline County to host ‘Carry the Light’ vigil for first responder suicide prevention on September 1
item.dc:creator: Shelli Poole
item.description: Community members, first responders, and local leaders will gather on the Saline County Courthouse lawn next month for “Carry the Light,” an event dedicated to first responder suicide prevention and remembrance. Scheduled for Tuesday, Sept. 1, 2026, the evening aims to honor those lost, support those currently struggling, and foster a supportive community where seeking […]
item.content:encoded:
Community members, first responders, and local leaders will gather on the Saline County Courthouse lawn next month for “Carry the Light,” an event dedicated to first responder suicide prevention and remembrance. Scheduled for Tuesday, Sept. 1, 2026, the evening aims to honor those lost, support those currently struggling, and foster a supportive community where seeking help is viewed as a sign of strength. Read more below.




The gathering, which begins at 6:30 p.m., will formally recognize Sept. 1 as First Responder Suicide Prevention Day. The program will include the presentation of official proclamations recognizing the day at both the state and county levels.

For event organizer Serena Krone, the date carries a deeply personal significance. Her sister, Brittany Wildhaber, a volunteer firefighter and EMT, died by suicide on Sept. 1, 2017.

“For nine years, September 1 has represented one of the darkest days of my life,” Krone said. “I can’t change what happened that day, but I can help change what this day means going forward. My hope is that September 1 becomes a day when we remember those we’ve lost while reminding the first responders who are still here that they matter, they are needed, and they never have to carry the weight of this job alone.”

A central portion of the evening will be the symbolic “Carry the Light” candle observance. Attendees will carry candles representing both remembrance and hope, honoring the departed while showing solidarity with active first responders who face unseen struggles.

“Sometimes someone can’t see the light for themselves,” Krone noted. “In those moments, we have to be willing to carry it for them until they can see it again.”

The event is open to the public and is designed to bring together firefighters, EMS professionals, law enforcement officers, dispatchers, their families, elected officials, and the broader Saline County community. Organizers emphasize that the public’s presence serves as a powerful demonstration of support for the men and women who spend their lives responding to emergencies.

item.content:encoded:
The Saline Home Builders Association is preparing to host its 2026 “Fore the Builders” Golf Tournament on Thursday, Sept. 17, at the Hurricane Golf & Country Club.

The upcoming community event features two separate flights, meals for participants, and various prize opportunities. Read more below.




The tournament will host two scheduled flights for teams. Morning participants can check in and enjoy breakfast during the 8 a.m. registration period, with the first flight officially teeing off at 8:30 a.m.

Afternoon players will have a separate registration and lunch starting at noon, followed by the second flight at 1 p.m.

The team entry fee is set at $450. Additionally, attendees can purchase a separate game package for $60. The tournament will conclude with the distribution of prizes and awards to the participating golfers.

Those interested in registering a team or seeking further information about the event can contact Amy with the Saline Home Builders Association by calling 501-909-8055 or emailing salinehba@gmail.com.

item.title: Saline County Flea Market and Trade Day is set for Aug 15th at Fairgrounds
item.dc:creator: Shelli Poole
item.description: The Saline County Fair Association is hosting its fourth Flea Market and Trade Day on Saturday, August 15, offering a diverse array of local merchandise, crafts, and food. Proceeds from this free event will directly fund ongoing efforts to rebuild and improve the Saline County Fairgrounds. Read more below. The community fundraiser, themed “Rebuilding Together,” […]
item.content:encoded:
The Saline County Fair Association is hosting its fourth Flea Market and Trade Day on Saturday, August 15, offering a diverse array of local merchandise, crafts, and food.

Proceeds from this free event will directly fund ongoing efforts to rebuild and improve the Saline County Fairgrounds. Read more below.




The community fundraiser, themed “Rebuilding Together,” is 7:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. at the Fairgrounds, at 406 Fairfield in Benton. The event will take place rain or shine, because the indoor vendor buildings are fully air-conditioned.

Shoppers can expect to find a wide variety of goods, including:

  • yard sale items,
  • flea market finds,
  • crafts,
  • antiques,
  • fresh produce,
  • eggs,
  • animals, and
  • animal supplies.

Come hungry,  because the Homemakers Extension kitchen and concession stand will be open, serving a variety of foods and treats to raise additional funds for the rebuilding project.

If you’d like to be a vendor, indoor and outdoor vendor spaces are still available. A 12×12-foot outside space costs $25, while a 10×10-foot inside space is $50. The spaces do not include tents, tables, chairs, electricity, or water, and all booth rental proceeds go directly toward the fairgrounds.

Vendor setup is scheduled for Friday evening from 4:30-7:00 p.m., and Saturday morning at 6:00 a.m. Participating businesses are required to meet all standard licensing requirements, and animal vendors must comply with applicable regulations.

Upcoming Flea Market and Trade Days are scheduled for September 26, October 24, and a two-day event on November 6 and 7. Interested vendors or attendees can request  information by texting 501-860-3101, emailing salinecofair@hotmail.com, or visiting the association’s online registration form.

item.title: Benton cancels August Third Thursday event due to extreme heat forecast
item.dc:creator: Shelli Poole
item.description: Organizers of Downtown Benton’s Third Thursday have announced the cancellation of their upcoming August 20, 2026, event due to a prolonged forecast of intense heat. With triple-digit temperatures and dangerous heat indexes expected over the next ten-plus days, officials stated the difficult decision was made to ensure the safety of the community. Read more […]
item.content:encoded:
Organizers of Downtown Benton’s Third Thursday have announced the cancellation of their upcoming August 20, 2026, event due to a prolonged forecast of intense heat. With triple-digit temperatures and dangerous heat indexes expected over the next ten-plus days, officials stated the difficult decision was made to ensure the safety of the community. Read more below.




In a public statement, event organizers explained that keeping vendors, food truck operators, musical bands, and local citizens safe is their top priority. The excessive temperatures and high heat indexes made canceling the outdoor summer celebration a necessary precaution to prevent heat-related illnesses among attendees and workers.

While the August festivities are canceled, the popular downtown festival will resume next month. Organizers confirmed the community gathering will return in September for its scheduled “Faith and Family” night, and they urge everyone to stay safe and cool in the meantime.

item.content:encoded:
Join Saline County History & Heritage Society (SCHHS) for the 40th anniversary celebration on August 13th. Read more below.




Come to commemorate the inception of the SCHHS back in 1986 as a nonprofit – preserving, researching, and exploring the history and heritage of our Saline County community.

The fun is on Thursday, August 13. The program begins at 5:00 p.m. at 123 North Market St.

Show your support for history by attending this presentation, and bring a friend. There’s no charge to attend, and guests are welcome.

However, if you’d like to become a supporting member of the SCHHS, it’s $25 per year per household which helps to sustain our non-profit in educating the community on the county’s history, preservation of our great heritage, and providing a space for research.

item.title: Guys and Dolls musical coming to Benton’s Royal Theatre Aug 13-23
item.dc:creator: Shelli Poole
item.description: The Royal Theatre in downtown Benton will bring the classic Broadway musical “Guys and Dolls” to the local stage this August. The upcoming production, sponsored by Meridiem Psychological Services Inc., will run for two weekends from August 13-23. The 150-minute show transports audiences from the bright lights of New York City to the cafes of […]
item.content:encoded:
The Royal Theatre in downtown Benton will bring the classic Broadway musical “Guys and Dolls” to the local stage this August. The upcoming production, sponsored by Meridiem Psychological Services Inc., will run for two weekends from August 13-23.




The 150-minute show transports audiences from the bright lights of New York City to the cafes of Havana, Cuba.

The plot follows the intertwined stories of gamblers Nathan Detroit and Sky Masterson, along with their respective love interests, nightclub performer Miss Adelaide and straight-laced missionary Sarah Brown.

Evening performances are scheduled for Thursdays, Fridays, and Saturdays at 7 p.m., while Sunday matinees will begin at 2 p.m.

Local actors lead the cast, featuring Sa’Teh Abdul as Nathan Detroit, Skyla Conger as Miss Adelaide, Chase Albaugh as Sky Masterson, and Emma Guill as Sarah Brown.

The creative team includes director Matthew Burns, musical director Lexie Ellis, and choreographer Reagan Hammonds Turbyfill.

General admission tickets are $20 online or $22 at the box office, with discounted rates available for seniors 60 and older, college students, military personnel, and students in 12th grade and younger.

Theater officials at the 111 S. Market Street venue advise patrons to purchase tickets in advance, noting that the PG-13 rated production includes strobe lights, haze effects, and simulated gunshots.

Read more information at https://onthestage.tickets/show/the-royal-theatre/696a6b55a201b7335f7a26c9/.

Sponsored by Ridout Lumber Company and Saline County Home Builders Association, the event is set for Thursday, October 15th at the Hill Barn Event Center on 100 Hill Road in Bryant. That’s off Reynolds Road and adjacent to Hill Barn Elementary School.

Doors open at 6PM, dinner and show begins at 7PM and the auctions and casino games continue the evening at 8PM.

Watch for information on tickets and more at https://habitatsalinecounty.com/.

item.title: Free beginner beekeeping workshop Tuesday at the Fairgrounds
item.dc:creator: Shelli Poole
item.description: Residents interested in learning the art of apiculture are invited to attend a free introductory beekeeping workshop at the Saline County Fairgrounds this August. The event will offer beginners a comprehensive overview of the practice, led by local experts from Southern Yankee Homestead. Read more below. The workshop is scheduled to take place on Tuesday, […]
item.content:encoded:
Residents interested in learning the art of apiculture are invited to attend a free introductory beekeeping workshop at the Saline County Fairgrounds this August.

The event will offer beginners a comprehensive overview of the practice, led by local experts from Southern Yankee Homestead. Read more below.




The workshop is scheduled to take place on Tuesday, August 18th, beginning at 6 p.m. at the Saline County Fairgrounds.

Hosted by Southern Yankee Homestead, this educational session is tailored specifically for beginners with little to no prior experience. Instructors will guide attendees through the fundamental basics of beekeeping, providing the foundational knowledge needed to safely start and maintain a healthy bee colony.

Admission to the workshop is completely FREE and open to the public. Anyone interested in attending or seeking more information about the event is encouraged to call or text the organizers at 501-860-3773.
